title: Grateful Dead Live at Winterland Arena on 1970-04-15
lineage: SBD > MR > DAT > CD > EAC > mkwACT > SHN

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture of a spring‑1970 classic, driven by the legendary Cryptical > Drums > Jam > The Other One sequence and an electrifying Lovelight/NFA/Lovelight sandwich.
ai_review.review: This tape is praised for its pristine, almost studio‑quality soundboard mix that lets every instrument shine.  The performance is a tour de force of 1970 Dead energy – the mind‑blowing Cryptical‑Drums‑Jam into The Other One, the soaring Lovelight/NFA/Lovelight sandwich and scorching versions of Man’s World, Candyman, Dancin' and Dire Wolf all receive rave notices.  Minor blemishes (a missing China Cat > I Know You Rider segment and a cut in Hard to Handle) do not detract from what most reviewers call an essential, near‑perfect show.

ai_rating.rationale: Overwhelmingly positive reviews (mostly 5‑star) highlight both superb soundboard fidelity and an extraordinary musical performance; only a few minor complaints about missing tracks keep the rating just shy of perfect.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clear mix with superb instrument separation; reviewers repeatedly call it “like being onstage”.  Occasional issues: a fade‑out in Hard to Handle and the absence of China Cat > I Know You Rider.

standout_songs: Cryptical Envelopment → Drums → Jam → The Other One
poor_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider (missing)
show_quality.setlist_flow: Reviewers love the seamless flow from Cryptical into the drum‑jam and The Other One, then into Dire Wolf, and later the Lovelight/NFA/Lovelight sandwich; energy stays high throughout with tight segues.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly described as ‘wailing’, ‘smoking’, with perfect tone and deliberate, creative playing.
band_member_comments.Phil: Praised for a thundering bass foundation on The Other One and grooving support across the set.
band_member_comments.Bob: Mentioned mainly in vocal exchanges during Lovelight/NFA; no strong criticism, just noted as part of the mix.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith Godchaux’s tasteful piano/organ work is highlighted positively; a single reviewer disparages Brent but most focus on Keith’s contribution.
band_member_comments.Drums: The cryptical drum solo and mid‑drum jam are repeatedly called “astonishing”, “powerful” and a key highlight of the show.
